---
title: "Day coverage and overlapping intervals"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Day coverage and overlapping intervals}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

The synthetic UTF-8 export bundled as `extdata/audit-line-meta.txt` contains six line records and one meta event. The six start/end offsets in seconds after local midnight are (0,10), (0,10), (0,6), (4,10), (3,7), and (6,14). Each row names a different example app. The following date has a line header with an empty body.

```{r}
library(appusageR)
path <- system.file("extdata", "audit-line-meta.txt", package = "appusageR")
first <- run_first_level_appusage(path, participant_id = "demo", strict = TRUE)
second <- run_second_level_appusage(first)
window <- as.Date(c("2024-10-08", "2024-10-10"))
observed <- audit_appusage_days(second, window = window)
zero <- audit_appusage_days(second, window = window, strategy = "zero_window")
observed$calendar
c(recorded_mean_ms = observed$mean_ms, window_mean_ms = zero$mean_ms)
stopifnot(observed$denominator_days == 1, zero$denominator_days == 3,
          observed$numerator_ms == 44000, zero$numerator_ms == 44000)
```

The 8 October numerator sums the six saved durations. Including 9 October (empty header) and 10 October (absent header) as zero changes the denominator to three. The default keeps the two blank days out of the mean. The event component supplies its own coverage evidence.

```{r}
audit_appusage_days(second, component = "meta_events", window = window)$calendar
overlap <- audit_appusage_overlap(second)
overlap$pairs
overlap$daily
stopifnot(all(overlap$pairs$total > 0), overlap$totals[["endpoint_union"]] == 14000)
x <- second$data$episode
plot(c(0, 14), c(1, nrow(x)), type = "n", ylab = "Example record",
     xlab = "Seconds since first start")
origin <- min(x$start_ts_ms)
segments((x$start_ts_ms - origin) / 1000, seq_len(nrow(x)),
         (x$end_ts_ms - origin) / 1000, seq_len(nrow(x)), lwd = 3)
```

The endpoints cover 14 seconds. The sum of spans is 44 seconds and the excess is 30 seconds. Pair counts describe geometry. The optional allocation views assign time across the full set of intervals under an explicit assumption.

```{r}
allocation <- audit_appusage_overlap(second, strategy = "equal_share")
allocation$view[[1]]
priority <- sort(unique(x$package_name))
audit_appusage_overlap(second, strategy = "priority", priority = priority)$view[[1]]
```

For a mapped interval table, supply millisecond epoch values and declare their original representation. The example below uses displayed minute boundaries and a positive saved duration in the same minute. That row contributes to the stored-duration total. It has no positive endpoint span. Unknown applications leave shared slices unassigned when included in the analysis.

```{r}
mapped <- data.frame(start_ts_ms = c(0, 0, 60000, 60000),
                     end_ts_ms = c(120000, 60000, 120000, 60000),
                     duration_ms = c(100000, 30000, 45000, 1200),
                     package_name = c("example.a", "example.a", NA, "example.b"),
                     activity_type = "foreground")
view <- audit_appusage_overlap(mapped, precision = "display_minute",
                              strategy = "equal_share", tz = "UTC",
                              include_collection_app = TRUE)
view$row_status
view$view[[1]]
```
